title: A PKCE pair
description:
Make the code verifier and challenge used by OAuth's PKCE.

```
verifier:  dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk
challenge: E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM
check with RFC 7636's example: True
```

starter.main.py:

print(challenge("dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk") == "E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM")

hints: The standard `secrets` module makes random values that are safe for secrets (the `random` module is not). `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` returns 32 random bytes as base64url text without padding: 43 characters, all of them allowed in a verifier.
requirements: `challenge(verifier)` is the SHA-256 of the verifier, base64url-encoded without `=` padding.
Check `challenge` against the example in RFC 7636 (the verifier and challenge above).
stretch: Build the full authorisation URL with `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `state`, `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256`.
